population_boundary: Human intracranial (ECoG, sEEG, depth, intracortical) decoders of imagined, covert or inner speech; attempted speech by paralysed participants (Guenther 2009, Brumberg 2011), scalp EEG/MEG, listening-only and overt-only studies are outside. Priors: first public before 2015-11; [concurrent] 2015-11 to 2016-11. Same boundary for every audited slot.

inherited.M01: Auditory-cued word repetition task (listen, imagine hearing, repeat) from the Pei 2011 / Martin 2014 ECoG covert-repetition lineage.
inherited.M02: Instructed word labels only; no training-only auxiliary signal.
inherited.M03: Per-subject offline training with inner leave-one-out grid search and training-fold discriminative-power weighting.
inherited.M04: Cued 'imagine hearing' of a just-heard word, paired with listening and overt repetition of the same item (paired-overt covert design, Pei 2011 lineage).
inherited.M05: Clinical subdural ECoG in 5 epilepsy patients, high-gamma 70-150 Hz envelopes (Leuthardt / Pei / Martin 2014 lineage).
inherited.M11: Instructed item identity, imagined epochs at cue onset (no measured imagery onset).

topics.inclusion_rule: Same intracranial imagined-speech decoder population as the published M06/M12 topics (pattern below). Design of interest: how the decoder handles trial-to-trial timing variability of imagined trials: time-averaged or fixed-window features, lagged linear model, sequence model (HMM), or explicit temporal alignment (DTW or another warping) inside the classifier. Boundary: DTW used only to align a decoded output with a reference for scoring (Pasley 2012, Martin 2014) is evaluation (M11/M12), not decoder alignment.
topics.metric: imagined-speech classification accuracy relative to chance; higher is better

topics.inclusion_rule: Same population. Design of interest: the decoded output unit for imagined trials: rest vs task, phoneme or vowel class, consonant class, whole-word identity, continuous acoustic features, sentence text. Boundary: word stimuli whose sub-word units are classified (Pei 2011) count as sub-word output.
topics.metric: imagined-speech classification accuracy relative to chance
